subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: What public foreground scheduler contract should OpenClaw expose for multi-agent deployments: per-agent lanes, agent-group lanes, workload lanes, or a unified lane-classification model?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but fixing it adds public config and runtime scheduling semantics that must coordinate with hook, subagent, browser/workload, and aggregate-cap safety work.

options.title: Design unified scheduler lanes
options.body: Add one server-owned lane-classification model that can express per-agent or agent-group isolation while preserving a global resource cap and default shared-main behavior.

options.title: Narrow to per-agent foreground lanes
options.body: Add only an additive per-agent foreground lane config now, leaving browser, hook, and subagent lanes to separate APIs.

options.title: Defer to adjacent lane work
options.body: Keep this open as evidence while maintainers first settle the narrower hook and subagent lane proposals.

recommendation.title: Design unified scheduler lanes
recommendation.body: Add one server-owned lane-classification model that can express per-agent or agent-group isolation while preserving a global resource cap and default shared-main behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal runs through the gateway lane setup and embedded runtime queue composition that define this product surface.
